question: What is another common name for cancellous bone?

options.A: Cortical bone
options.B: Compact bone
options.C: Spongy bone
options.D: Dense bone

explanation: You got this! Cancellous bone is often called spongy bone because if you look at it inside, it has a porous, honeycomb-like pattern just like a kitchen sponge.

question: What is the main job of GABA in the central nervous system?

options.A: It builds strong protective membranes around nerve cells
options.B: It speeds up heart rate during emergency physical stress
options.C: It acts as the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter to calm brain activity
options.D: It carries oxygen directly to neurons in the frontal lobe

explanation: GABA is basically the brain's natural calming chemical or 'brake pedal'. It slows down nerve signals so the brain doesn't get overloaded with too much electrical excitement.

question: What is the main goal when treating a patient who has amenorrhoea?

options.A: Surgically removing the ovaries to stop hormone swings
options.B: Immediately restoring natural fertility in every case
options.C: Treating the specific underlying root cause
options.D: Preventing future pregnancy with strong contraceptives

explanation: Because amenorrhoea is a sign of something else, our treatment focuses on fixing the root problem—whether it is lifestyle, hormones, or anatomy.

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient after inserting a retention suppository?

options.A: Drink two liters of ice-cold water within five minutes
options.B: Force an immediate bowel movement to test if it worked
options.C: Try to remain lying down and hold the medication for 15 to 30 minutes
options.D: Get up immediately and walk briskly around the hospital hallway

explanation: Giving the medication time to dissolve and absorb into the mucosal lining prevents it from being prematurely expelled. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: What advice should a nurse give to help a patient maintain healthy vaginal flora?

options.A: Use scented soaps daily inside the vaginal canal for deep cleaning.
options.B: Wear tight synthetic underwear to keep the area dry.
options.C: Avoid harsh vaginal douches that disrupt protective bacteria.
options.D: Stop taking prescribed antibiotics as soon as itching stops.

explanation: Fantastic! Douching washes away the good bacteria (lactobacilli) and messes with natural pH, making it way easier for bad germs and yeast to take over.

question: Why must nurses look at published research with a critical eye?

options.A: Research studies are only meant for academic promotion
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to rewrite journal articles
options.C: Authors purposely hide their results to confuse readers
options.D: Not all published studies are designed or conducted well

explanation: Even peer-reviewed journals can contain flaws, so nurses must evaluate the evidence before applying it to patients. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) when treating erectile dysfunction?

options.A: Increasing red blood cell production
options.B: Lowering systemic body temperature
options.C: Relaxing the muscles in the bladder
options.D: Enhancing blood flow to penile tissues

explanation: Awesome! These meds relax smooth muscles so blood can flow easily into the penis when the patient is stimulated.

question: Why do healthcare workers need to do an N95 fit test every year?

options.A: Weight changes or dental work can change how the mask seals
options.B: Manufacturers change their plastic formulas yearly
options.C: Hospital rules just want to renew licenses
options.D: Filters expire chemically after one year

explanation: Our faces change over time! A fit test ensures your mask still seals safely against your unique face shape.

question: Why is it so important for young neurons to migrate to new locations in the developing brain?

options.A: It prevents neurons from dividing too quickly inside the spinal canal
options.B: It directly creates the protective myelin covering around nerve fibers
options.C: It seals the neural tube to prevent fluid leakage
options.D: It ensures that neurons reach their correct final locations to form functional layers

explanation: You got it! Neurons must travel from where they are born to their precise final spots so the brain can build its proper layered structure.

question: Why is it helpful to involve local and religious leaders in community campaigns against harmful scarification?

options.A: They manage the hospital budget for rural health clinics
options.B: They are trained medical doctors who can prescribe antibiotics
options.C: They hold strong influence over community beliefs and behaviors
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to use surgical scalpels

explanation: Correct! Community leaders shape public opinion and can truly help guide their people toward healthier, safer lifestyle choices.

question: Why might a clinically successful hospital treatment fail once the patient goes home?

options.A: Hospital laboratories are always more accurate than home testing
options.B: The patient's home environment and social support were ignored
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for home use
options.D: Nurses fail to document the discharge date properly

explanation: If a care plan does not fit a patient's real-life social and financial situation at home, they will struggle to follow it. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are gravies and sauces often added to meats on a soft diet?

options.A: To hide the taste of spoiled ingredients in the kitchen
options.B: To add moisture and prevent the meat from feeling dry during chewing
options.C: To change the color of the food to stimulate appetite
options.D: To dramatically increase the sodium content for hydration

explanation: Soft meats can easily become dry and difficult to swallow; gravies provide necessary lubrication. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h4)

question: What does a high Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) level mostly point toward?

options.A: Severe acute viral hepatitis infection
options.B: Chronic kidney filtration failure
options.C: Bile duct obstruction or bone activity
options.D: Massive breakdown of red blood cells

explanation: Brilliant! ALP hangs out in the bile ducts and bones, so high numbers usually point your clinical suspicion toward biliary issues or bone growth/turnover.

question: Which of these statements about nursing leadership is FALSE?

options.A: It is built by taking on small projects and precepting students.
options.B: It is a continuous developmental journey throughout a career.
options.C: It can be cultivated through mentorship and continuing education.
options.D: It is an innate trait that cannot be learned or improved over time.

explanation: Leadership isn't a rare magic power you are born with! Anyone can grow and improve their leadership skills over time through practice, learning, and good mentors.

question: What should you do first if you spot an unexplained, non-healing sore on a patient's tongue?

options.A: Scrape the surface firmly to see if it bleeds like thrush
options.B: Prescribe an antibacterial mouthwash for two weeks
options.C: Document its exact size, shape, and refer for medical evaluation
options.D: Advise the patient to stop using commercial toothpaste

explanation: Always record clear details of the lesion and send the patient for a proper medical review to rule out anything serious.

question: What is the biggest benefit of practicing complex procedures on high-tech manikins in the simulation lab?

options.A: It removes the need for faculty members to observe student performance.
options.B: It completely replaces the need for written examinations in nursing school.
options.C: It guarantees that students will never make a mistake in the actual hospital.
options.D: Students can practice high-risk procedures without risking patient safety.

explanation: Simulation gives you a safe space to build confidence and master your hands-on skills before you ever touch a real patient. Brilliant learning environment!

question: How does missing one fallopian tube generally affect a woman's chances of getting pregnant naturally?

options.A: The patient will instantly experience early surgical menopause
options.B: Pregnancy is still possible because the remaining tube can function
options.C: Natural conception is completely impossible without medical help
options.D: Ectopic pregnancies will occur in every single attempted cycle

explanation: Wonderful news for patients! One healthy tube is often all it takes to capture an egg and achieve a natural pregnancy.

question: Which common bacterium is most often linked to duodenal ulcers?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Helicobacter pylori
options.D: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation: Spot on! Helicobacter pylori (or H. pylori) is a tough little spiral bacterium that sneaks under the protective mucus layer of the stomach and duodenum, causing sores.

question: How does a nurse apply the principle of justice on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: By ignoring minor complaints from elderly clients to focus on wealthy individuals
options.B: By spending the entire shift caring only for clients who pay extra hospital fees
options.C: By providing equal and fair quality care to every assigned client regardless of background
options.D: By refusing to admit clients who belong to a different religious group

explanation: Justice means treating all clients fairly and equitably without bias or discrimination based on their social status. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h2)

question: Why can frequent use of high-strength spermicide sometimes increase the risk of infections?

options.A: It permanently paralyzes the immune cells in the bloodstream
options.B: It neutralizes all normal vaginal flora leaving the body dry
options.C: It can cause tiny cuts in vaginal tissue that let viruses enter
options.D: It reacts with air to create toxic gases inside the pelvis

explanation: That's right! Chemical irritation from overuse can break down natural tissue defenses, making it easier for infections to slip in.

question: Why do patients sometimes resist following a nursing care plan?

options.A: Fear, misunderstanding, or a perceived loss of personal control
options.B: An excessive desire to follow medical instructions perfectly
options.C: Complete agreement with the community nurse
options.D: Too much free time available during the day

explanation: Resistance is usually just fear or a worry that they are losing their independence. Once you understand that, it's easier to help them!

question: Why is family planning counseling a key part of post-abortion care?

options.A: To ensure the client conceives again within the next month
options.B: To fulfill a hospital administrative requirement unrelated to health
options.C: To help the client prevent future unintended pregnancies and repeat procedures
options.D: To punish the client for experiencing a pregnancy loss

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps clients protect their health and avoid another unplanned pregnancy down the line. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Why is it so important to respect local customs and beliefs when doing home visits?

options.A: Nurses are legally required to practice traditional medicine first
options.B: Traditional beliefs strongly influence local health practices and family acceptance
options.C: Hospitals have no influence over community health traditions
options.D: Foreign donors demand strict adherence to local customs

explanation: When you respect people's traditions, they trust you more. This openness stops families from hiding things from you and helps them accept helpful health advice.

question: What is venepuncture primarily used for in clinical practice?

options.A: Withdrawing blood for diagnostic testing
options.B: Checking lung function capacity
options.C: Assessing electrical heart activity
options.D: Measuring deep body temperature

explanation: Venepuncture involves piercing a vein to collect blood samples needed for various laboratory investigations. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: How do diuretic medications generally help the body get rid of extra water?

options.A: By destroying waste products in the renal cortex
options.B: By increasing blood flow directly to the glomerulus
options.C: By stopping the production of water in the liver
options.D: By blocking sodium reabsorption in the nephron

explanation: Think of diuretics as helpers that stop the nephron from reabsorbing sodium. Water naturally follows sodium, so both stay in the urine and leave the body!

question: Why must you always lower a hospital bed to its lowest position after finishing a bed change?

options.A: To comply with fire safety codes for emergency exits
options.B: To reduce the risk of injury if the patient tries to get out of bed
options.C: To allow the mechanical bed motor to cool down
options.D: To make it easier for the cleaning crew to mop underneath

explanation: You got it! A low bed minimizes the fall distance if an unassisted patient tries to climb out, protecting them from serious head injuries or broken bones.

question: Which of the following is an example of an adaptive coping mechanism for a newly diagnosed HIV patient?

options.A: Turning to heavy alcohol use to forget the diagnosis
options.B: Denying the existence of the virus and skipping clinic visits
options.C: Joining a peer support group and talking with a counsellor
options.D: Isolating oneself completely from all human contact

explanation: Seeking community support and professional guidance helps patients process their diagnosis in a healthy, constructive manner. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: What legal document can a court issue to stop an abuser from coming near a survivor?

options.A: A business license
options.B: A property deed
options.C: A protection order
options.D: A tax clearance certificate

explanation: Correct! A protection order legally restrains an abuser from contacting or coming close to the survivor.

question: Why do nurses keep their feet wide apart when lifting a patient?

options.A: To reduce pressure on the knees
options.B: To create a stable base of support
options.C: To stretch the hamstring muscles
options.D: To increase speed during the transfer

explanation: Spreading your feet gives you great balance and keeps you steady, so you don't easily lose your footing while helping a patient. You've got this!

question: Which of the following is a common systemic challenge faced by maternal care teams in low-resource settings?

options.A: Mandatory retirement for midwives at age thirty
options.B: Zero workload and extremely short working hours
options.C: Staff shortages and lack of functional equipment
options.D: An excessive surplus of modern diagnostic machines

explanation: In many under-resourced settings, frontline health workers battle daily with personnel deficits and broken equipment. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h8)

question: What dangerous drug interaction must you warn patients about when taking ED meds like sildenafil (Viagra)?

options.A: Taking them with dairy products causes permanent blindness
options.B: Combining them with organic nitrates causes severe hypotension
options.C: Swallowing them with fruit juice stops their absorption entirely
options.D: Mixing them with aspirin causes sudden kidney failure

explanation: This is a classic clinical pearl! Both nitrates (for heart pain) and PDE5 inhibitors drop blood pressure. Taking them together can cause a life-threatening crash.

question: Why do patients with heart valve problems often develop a heart murmur?

options.A: The electrical wires in the heart rub against each other.
options.B: Turbulent blood flow occurs as blood moves through narrowed or leaky valves.
options.C: Air gets trapped inside the heart muscle tissue.
options.D: The lungs make whistling sounds during deep breathing.

explanation: Normally, blood flows smoothly and quietly. But when it's forced through a tight or leaky valve, it splashes around and makes a WHOOSH sound—which we call a murmur!

question: A nurse needs a quick estimate of a patient's daily calorie needs without special gas-exchange equipment. What is best to use?

options.A: A validated predictive equation like the Mifflin-St Jeor formula
options.B: A laboratory blood test measuring thyroid antibody levels
options.C: A direct calorimetry thermal chamber room
options.D: A 24-hour continuous core body temperature recording

explanation: When fancy equipment isn't around, clinical formulas using age, weight, and height give us a fast, reliable estimate of calorie needs.

question: When is compromising a better choice than collaborating?

options.A: When unlimited time is available for deep discussion
options.B: When time is limited and a quick middle ground is needed
options.C: When patient safety is directly and immediately threatened
options.D: When neither party cares about the final outcome

explanation: When you are rushed on the ward and don't have hours to talk things through, splitting the difference (compromising) is a fast, practical fix.

question: Why should nurses approach patient non-compliance with empathy instead of anger?

options.A: Because pharmaceutical companies require nurses to defend poor patient habits
options.B: Because judgmental attitudes automatically make patients immune to prescription drugs
options.C: Because non-compliance is usually driven by complex underlying barriers rather than simple defiance
options.D: Because hospital policies prohibit nurses from correcting patients who miss doses

explanation: Spot on! When we look past the surface, we find real struggles like high costs or confusion—not stubbornness.

question: Why must patients take off all jewelry and metal objects before a CT scan?

options.A: Metal attracts the magnetic radiation from the machine
options.B: Metal heats up dangerously during the scan process
options.C: Metal objects cause artifact streaks on the images
options.D: Metal interferes with the hospital Wi-Fi signals

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely and creates ugly, bright streaks on the scan that can hide important details. Always good to remember in clinicals!

question: What kind of air pressure is kept inside the operating room to keep outside air from rushing in?

options.A: Vacuum pressure
options.B: Positive pressure
options.C: Negative pressure
options.D: Neutral atmospheric pressure

explanation: That's right! Positive pressure gently pushes air outwards whenever the door opens, stopping hallway germs from drifting in.

question: A patient with sickle cell anaemia is admitted in a painful vaso-occlusive crisis. Which immediate nursing intervention should be prioritized?

options.A: Preparing the patient for immediate surgical removal of the spleen
options.B: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload in the lungs
options.C: Administering prescribed pain medication and encouraging fluids
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to improve circulation

explanation: Managing pain and rehydrating the patient to thin the blood and restore circulation are the immediate priorities during an acute crisis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: How does a high Total Fertility Rate affect local healthcare facilities?

options.A: It reduces the need for community health education programs
options.B: It immediately lowers the prevalence of infectious diseases
options.C: It strains maternal and pediatric wards due to high patient volumes
options.D: It guarantees an abundance of specialized nursing staff in clinics

explanation: High birth rates bring immense joy, but they also mean packed maternity wards and busy pediatric clinics that can easily stretch a hospital's resources thin.

question: Why does MBO help improve staff morale in a nursing unit?

options.A: Because supervisors stop visiting the clinical areas
options.B: Because salaries are automatically doubled every month
options.C: Because nurses have a voice in setting their targets
options.D: Because it removes all heavy workloads from the ward

explanation: Involving staff in decision-making gives them a sense of ownership, which boosts workplace morale. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to social services for persons with disabilities?

options.A: Cultural stigma and negative beliefs about disability
options.B: Poverty and lack of financial resources for transportation
options.C: Bureaucratic hurdles in welfare offices

question: What is the minimum recommended time for washing hands with soap and water?

options.A: 20 seconds
options.B: 2 minutes
options.C: 10 seconds

question: Which of these everyday body activities is managed by an autonomic reflex?

options.A: Reaching out to pick up a stethoscope
options.B: Deliberate walking across a hospital room
options.C: Changes in heart rate and blood pressure
options.D: Writing patient notes in a chart

explanation: Spot on! Autonomic reflexes quietly run your automatic internal functions—like heart rate and digestion—so you don't have to think about them.

question: A toddler arrives at the emergency unit suddenly drooling, making high-pitched breathing sounds (stridor), and very restless, but has no cough. What should you do first?

options.A: Keep the child calm and avoid invasive examinations
options.B: Immediately force the child to lie flat for an X-ray
options.C: Attempt to visualize the vocal cords with a tongue depressor
options.D: Administer oral fluids immediately to soothe the throat

explanation: This sounds like epiglottitis! If you upset or cry the child, their swollen airway can snap shut completely. Keep them calm in their mother's arms and don't force anything into their mouth.

question: When your clinical teacher watches you perform a sterile wound dressing, which domain of learning are they checking?

options.A: Theoretical memory recall
options.B: Cognitive domain only
options.C: Psychomotor domain
options.D: Affective domain exclusively

explanation: Dressing a wound is a physical, hands-on procedure, which falls squarely into the psychomotor domain. Hands-on practice makes perfect!

question: What does immediate contraceptive initiation mean in post-abortion care?

options.A: Starting pills only when the client feels severe pelvic pain

options.C: Waiting for three normal menstrual cycles before starting any method
options.D: Using barrier methods only after the follow-up appointment next month

explanation: Immediate initiation provides protection right away while the client is still at the healthcare facility, reducing the risk of an unremembered follow-up. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: As a nurse, what is your most critical intervention to catch energy imbalances early in hospitalized patients?

options.A: Restricting family visits during meals
options.B: Performing regular and accurate weight measurements
options.C: Asking the patient their favorite food
options.D: Administering a daily multivitamin

explanation: You've got this! Tracking weight trends over time is the most reliable way for a nurse to see if a patient's calorie intake is matching what their body needs.

question: Why do we advise pregnant mothers to eat small, frequent meals instead of three massive plates of food?

options.C: To prevent the stomach from becoming overly full and putting pressure on the sphincter
options.D: To stop the liver from producing excess bile during digestion

explanation: Smaller meals keep tummy pressure low, stopping acid from splashing up into the food pipe.

question: What is the primary reason governments get involved in the food supply?

options.A: To set the exact menu for every household
options.B: To protect public health and ensure stability
options.C: To control all farming businesses in the country
options.D: To eliminate the need for private grocery stores

explanation: Governments intervene primarily to safeguard the health and well-being of the population through safe and stable food systems. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: Why is asking about family and home life so important when assessing a patient with a skin rash?

options.A: It replaces the need for a physical skin examination
options.B: It helps identify if other household members share the same contact infection
options.C: It determines the exact antibiotic resistance profile of the organism

explanation: Contact infections love to bounce around families! Checking if others at home are scratching stops the vicious cycle of reinfection.

question: How does empowering clients help with everyday health advocacy?

options.A: It forces patients to follow strict hospital rules
options.B: It encourages patients to voice their preferences and choices
options.C: It removes the need for informed consent documents
options.D: It allows nurses to make medical decisions for the family

explanation: Exactly! When we empower patients, we give them the confidence and tools to speak up and take part in their own health choices.

question: Why do quality improvement projects usually start on a small scale instead of rolling out hospital-wide?

options.A: Hospital management does not care about patient safety on large wards
options.B: Small tests require no planning or financial investment
options.C: It ensures that no data is collected during the trial phase

explanation: Testing on a small scale lets you fix any bugs safely before introducing the new idea to the whole hospital.

question: Up to what gestational age is MVA typically performed in the first trimester?

options.A: 28 to 30 weeks
options.B: 12 to 14 weeks
options.C: 4 to 6 weeks
options.D: 20 to 22 weeks

explanation: MVA is designed and validated as a safe and effective procedure for early pregnancy loss and termination up to 12 to 14 weeks of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: How does early palliative care help a patient going through tough cancer treatments?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any surgical operations
options.B: It lowers hospital bills by shortening surgical procedures
options.C: It focuses on relieving symptoms, pain, and emotional distress
options.D: It guarantees that the cancer will completely disappear

explanation: Palliative care is all about comfort, helping patients manage tough physical and emotional symptoms every step of the way. You are doing wonderful work today!

question: Why is a teamwork (multidisciplinary) approach important for older adults' mental healthcare?

options.A: It allows the hospital to discharge the patient much faster

options.C: It ensures that nurses do not have to interact with the patient's family
options.D: It eliminates the need for any kind of medication therapy

explanation: Older patients often have medical, social, and emotional needs all at once, requiring different experts to team up. Teamwork makes the dream work!

question: In rehabilitation, what do we mean when we talk about setting SMART goals?

options.A: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
options.B: Safe, Medical, Active, Realistic, Team-oriented
options.C: Systematic, Managed, Assessed, Recorded, Tested
options.D: Simple, Meaningful, Accountable, Rapid, Targeted

explanation: SMART goals give patients and the healthcare team clear targets so everyone can see real progress being made day by day.

question: A patient arrives from a terrible car crash with massive internal bleeding. What must the trauma suite have ready immediately?

options.A: Cosmetic laser equipment and soothing music
options.B: Long-term recovery beds for overnight stays
options.C: Rapid blood transfusion equipment and crash carts

question: A patient has a worm infection. Which white blood cell count will likely be high on their lab results?

options.A: Eosinophils
options.B: Platelets

options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: Correct! Eosinophils are the specialists specialized in fighting off parasites and calming down allergic reactions.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: Taking over all daily tasks completely

options.C: Promoting independence, dignity, and safety
options.D: Confining the patient to strict bed rest

explanation: Nursing care aims to support the person's remaining abilities while keeping them safe and preserving their personal dignity. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is teaching family caregivers a key part of subacute discharge planning?

options.A: It allows family members to legally substitute for trained nurses
options.B: It removes the need for any follow-up visits with primary doctors
options.C: It ensures the facility receives additional government funding
options.D: It prepares them to safely manage medications and care tasks at home

explanation: You nailed it. Equipping family caregivers prevents slip-ups and keeps the patient from bouncing back to the hospital.

question: Why is it important to complete admission documentation promptly rather than waiting until the end of a long shift?

options.A: So that nurses can leave work before their shift officially ends
options.B: To allow the patient to take the paper home immediately
options.C: Because ward managers check handwriting speeds daily
options.D: To prevent forgetting important clinical details and ensure safety

explanation: Writing down observations immediately ensures accuracy and provides oncoming staff with up-to-date information for safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is hand hygiene still required after a nurse removes disposable medical gloves?

options.A: Soap chemically destroys the leftover rubber residue
options.B: Hospital policy requires double-washing regardless of gloves
options.C: Gloves do not protect against viral particles at all
options.D: Microbes can multiply rapidly inside gloves and hands can get contaminated

explanation: Warm, sweaty hands inside gloves create an ideal breeding ground for bacteria, making handwashing essential after removal. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why do doctors prescribe strong iodine solutions like Lugol's solution right before a thyroid surgery?

options.A: To prevent allergic reactions to general anesthesia agents

question: Which germs are the most common causes of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Candida albicans and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation: PID usually happens when sexually transmitted bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes. Always good to remember for clinicals!

question: When joints allow our bodies to move, what role do the bones play?

options.A: They create the pulling force

options.C: They produce lubricating fluid
options.D: They act as levers

question: A family member is too overwhelmed to understand a complex medical update. What is your best move as a nurse?

options.A: Repeat the complex medical terms more loudly
options.B: Hand out a detailed medical textbook to read
options.C: Ask the doctor to stop giving updates altogether

question: What is one of the biggest reasons operating room nurses experience mental burnout?

options.A: Having too many tea breaks during a single shift
options.B: Having zero paperwork or chart writing to do
options.C: The constant pressure and need to watch life-and-death details
options.D: Spending too many hours relaxing at a computer desk

explanation: Staying fully alert and focused during critical surgeries drains your emotional and mental energy. It is totally normal to feel tired, so self-care is vital!

question: What does 'asynchronous development' mean when talking about gifted children?

options.A: Language skills develop long before motor skills.
options.B: Physical growth happens much slower than in normal peers.
options.C: Intellectual, emotional, and physical ages do not match.
options.D: Emotional maturity always outpaces cognitive ability.

question: Which organ is primarily responsible for filtering and excreting water-soluble drug waste?

options.A: Kidneys
options.B: Lungs
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Skin

explanation: Your kidneys are your body's ultimate filters. They continuously clean your blood and flush out water-soluble drug breakdown products through your urine.

question: What do we call the spread of cancer cells to other parts of the body?

options.A: Carcinogenesis
options.B: Metastasis

options.D: Apoptosis

question: Which data collection method involves walking through the community to visually inspect environmental conditions?

question: Why do we encourage mothers to start breastfeeding right after birth?

options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions and helps milk production

question: What is a recommended nursing intervention to help prevent post-dural puncture headaches?

options.A: Encouraging adequate fluid intake
options.B: Massaging the lower back area
options.C: Keeping the patient walking for hours

question: How does popular media often misrepresent sexual intercourse to teenagers?

options.A: As casual, glamorous, and rarely involving negative consequences
options.B: As an activity that requires strict medical supervision
options.C: As something that only occurs among older adults
options.D: As an event that always results in immediate health complications

explanation: Media portrayals frequently glamorize sex while omitting discussions of contraception, consent, and infections, creating unrealistic expectations. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the most common active chemical found in modern spermicides?

options.A: Chlorhexidine
options.B: Hydrogen peroxide

options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

question: What actually opens the ion channels on a touch receptor when you press on the skin?

options.A: Physical stretching of the cell membrane
options.B: Hormonal changes in the blood
options.C: A drop in core body temperature
options.D: Electrical shocks from the brain

question: How does bovine mastitis (udder infection) directly affect raw milk?

options.A: It forces the cow to stop producing any milk permanently
options.B: It introduces pathogenic bacteria directly into the milk stream
options.C: It completely sterilizes the milk inside the udder gland
options.D: It increases the acid level enough to kill all other germs

explanation: Exactly! Mastitis means the cow's udder is infected, which unfortunately dumps disease-causing germs right into the milk as it's being produced.

question: Carbon monoxide causes chemical asphyxiation mainly because it:

options.A: Blocks the physical entry of air into the nose
options.B: Causes an immediate severe allergic reaction
options.C: Stops body cells from using oxygen properly
options.D: Crushes the chest wall from the outside

explanation: Even if someone is breathing normally, carbon monoxide sneaks in, binds to hemoglobin, and prevents cells from using oxygen. Tricky stuff, but you know it now!

question: What is a major danger of excessive cohesiveness in a healthcare team?

options.A: Groupthink, where dangerous errors might be ignored to keep peace
options.B: Complete lack of interest in patient outcomes
options.C: Constant fighting and failure to complete basic patient care tasks
options.D: Excessive individual competition among staff nurses

explanation: When teams become too cohesive, members may avoid speaking up against bad ideas to prevent conflict. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h4)

question: How does a nurse show client-centered care when planning a patient's rehab?

options.A: Involving the client and family in setting realistic daily personal goals
options.B: Following a rigid hospital routine without considering individual preferences
options.C: Deciding the discharge schedule without asking the client about their home setup
options.D: Focusing solely on physical therapy exercises prescribed by the doctor

explanation: Client-centered care means the patient and their family are part of the team, not just bystanders. When goals matter to them, they work harder to reach them!

question: If local currency drops sharply against foreign exchange rates, what pricing move should the DRF committee make?

options.A: Freezing all drug sales until the currency stabilizes completely
options.B: Reducing the retail price to encourage higher sales volume
options.C: Stopping all inventory audits for the next financial year
options.D: Transitioning to replacement-cost pricing to protect purchasing power

explanation: Smart move! Pegging your prices to current replacement costs ensures the money coming in actually matches today's market realities so you can restock without stress.

question: Why is activated charcoal often instilled right before the lavage tube is removed?

options.A: To lubricate the tube so it slips out of the throat without friction
options.B: To stimulate normal bowel movements and speed up total digestion
options.C: To neutralize any acidic cleaning fluids remaining in the stomach wall
options.D: To catch and bind any remaining toxin particles left behind in the gut

explanation: Charcoal binds tightly to residual toxins that escaped the physical washing process, preventing them from entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: A patient is admitted with right-sided heart failure. Which physical sign is the nurse most likely to spot?

options.A: Flushed, warm skin and bounding pulses
options.B: Sudden high fever and severe headache
options.C: Bulging neck veins and swollen ankles
options.D: Clear lung sounds with no breathing trouble

explanation: Right-sided failure causes fluid to back up into the rest of the body. You'll often see this as swollen legs and distended neck veins!

question: A community health nurse in rural Nigeria uses a mobile phone app to track children's immunizations. What does this show?

options.A: The integration of technology into modern community health practice
options.B: A complete return to medieval religious care giving methods
options.C: The abandonment of primary healthcare principles
options.D: An illegal practice that violates public health policies

explanation: Just like you using this CBT app on your phone, modern nurses use digital tools every day to make healthcare smarter and faster!

question: What is the job of beta-lactamase enzymes in bacterial cells?

options.A: By chemically breaking down the antibiotic structure
options.B: By physically blocking the cell wall pores
options.C: By absorbing the drug and storing it safely away
options.D: By tricking the drug into attacking healthy cells instead

explanation: Great job thinking through this! These enzymes act like tiny chemical scissors, cutting up and destroying the antibiotic before it can harm the bacterium. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h2)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to create a private, gentle setting during a perineal check?

options.A: Bright lighting interferes with visualizing superficial blood vessels
options.B: Perineal tissue is too fragile to touch without numbing agents
options.C: Patients frequently feel embarrassed about intimate examinations
options.D: Hospital policy strictly forbids family members from staying

explanation: Checking someone's private areas can feel very vulnerable. As a caring nurse, building trust and keeping things private helps your patient feel safe and respected.

question: A patient has swollen ankles. How should you advise them to position their legs when resting?

options.A: Dangling freely off the edge of the bed
options.B: Crossed tightly at the knees for stability
options.C: Flat on the floor while sitting in a chair
options.D: Elevated above the level of the heart

explanation: You've got this! Gravity is our helper here. Raising the legs higher than the heart lets trapped fluid flow smoothly back into circulation.

question: What is a key action public health nurses take to improve community nutrition?

options.A: Growing all the crops needed for the entire country inside hospitals
options.B: Organizing nutritional screenings and educating families on budget-friendly local meals
options.C: Passing strict laws to ban all processed foods globally
options.D: Taking over the management of international cargo shipping lines

explanation: Spot on! Nurses play a huge role by checking nutritional status and teaching families how to cook healthy, pocket-friendly local meals.

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge facing adolescent reproductive healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: Stigma and cultural views regarding teenage sexuality
options.B: Religious beliefs influencing family planning acceptance
options.C: Universal free access to all contraceptive supplies nationwide
options.D: Legal ambiguities surrounding minors and medical consent

explanation: Right! Contraceptives are definitely not free everywhere across Nigeria, making this statement false and the correct choice here. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h7)

question: What is a major challenge when conducting a longitudinal study in nursing research?

options.A: Higher risk of manipulating the independent variable by accident
options.B: Inability to ever observe changes over time
options.C: Participants dropping out over time, leading to missing data
options.D: Results are always available immediately within days

explanation: Spot on! Following people for months or years is tough because participants sometimes move away, lose interest, or drop out, which researchers call attrition.

question: Which common everyday drink should patients with anxiety and phobias cut back on because it triggers jitters and a fast heart rate?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Caffeine
options.C: Complex carbohydrates
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Caffeine is a stimulant. Too much coffee or energy drink can easily mimic or worsen panic symptoms like a racing pulse and shaky hands.

question: A nurse is about to start an intravenous line for a patient with no known infections. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Put on a heavy rubber apron and shoe covers
options.B: Move the patient to an airborne isolation room
options.C: Ask the patient to wear a surgical mask
options.D: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves

explanation: Standard precautions require hand hygiene and gloves before any procedure involving potential contact with blood or body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: What is the main reason for using aseptic technique during surgery?

options.A: To reduce the cost of surgical supplies
options.B: To make the surgical room smell clean
options.C: To eliminate all micro-organisms from the surgical field
options.D: To speed up the recovery time after anesthesia

explanation: Great job! Aseptic technique blocks germs and bad bugs from getting into the patient's vulnerable body tissues.

question: A nurse leaves the ward during a busy shift to run personal errands miles away and causes an accident. Who carries the blame?

options.A: The state nursing council
options.B: The hospital administration
options.C: The chief medical director
options.D: The nurse personally

explanation: Because the nurse was way out of bounds doing personal things away from work, the hospital escapes vicarious liability, leaving the nurse to face it alone.

question: Why should a nurse explain to a patient that antibiotics won't cure a regular viral cold?

options.A: Antibiotics immediately destroy nasal tissues
options.B: Viral infections always require surgical drainage
options.C: Viruses do not respond to antibacterial drugs
options.D: Antibiotics cause instant permanent deafness

explanation: You got it! Antibiotics only kill bacteria, so taking them for a virus won't help you feel better any faster.

question: What should be clearly recorded in the patient's register when a standing order is used?

options.A: The specific protocol used, assessment findings, and treatments given
options.B: The political affiliation of the patient receiving care
options.C: The personal home address of the facility's medical director
options.D: A detailed financial profit statement for the pharmacy unit

explanation: Proper documentation requires noting the exact protocol followed, clinical findings, and interventions administered for legal and continuity purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h7)

question: Chronic kidney disease is diagnosed in a pregnant woman if kidney trouble or protein in the urine is found before which gestational week?

options.A: Before fourteen weeks
options.B: Before ten weeks
options.C: Before thirty weeks
options.D: Before twenty weeks

explanation: Great to know! If signs show up before the twentieth week, it usually means the kidney issue was already there before the pregnancy started.

question: What does it mean to put research results into 'context'?

options.A: Translating the research report into three different languages
options.B: Comparing new study findings with past literature and clinical realities
options.C: Destroying old textbooks so staff only read the newest articles
options.D: Increasing the hospital budget to match the research costs

explanation: Contextualization just means looking at how new findings fit alongside existing science and whether they make sense on a busy ward.

question: Why is building therapeutic rapport so important before starting a psychosocial assessment?

options.A: It guarantees the client will take all prescribed medications on time.
options.B: It stops the client from ever feeling sad about their illness.
options.C: It helps the client feel safe enough to share honest personal feelings.
options.D: It allows the nurse to skip asking about family medical history.

explanation: Trust allows clients to lower their guard and discuss sensitive emotional and mental health topics openly with the nurse. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which animal is the main carrier of the Lassa virus?

options.A: Domestic house cat
options.B: Mastomys rat
options.C: Ground squirrel
options.D: Fruit bat

question: Which part of the ovary holds the developing egg follicles?

options.A: Medulla
options.B: Cortex

options.D: Fundus

question: How do public health nurses figure out how long a quarantine period should last for people exposed to a disease?

options.A: By waiting until laboratory cultures turn completely negative
options.B: By keeping contacts isolated for a standard seven days
options.C: By looking at the maximum incubation period of the disease

question: What exactly is a vesicovaginal fistula (VVF)?

options.A: An abnormal opening between the bladder and the vagina

options.C: A complete failure of the kidneys to produce urine
options.D: An infection of the lining inside the urinary bladder

question: What is the clock-face method used for during mealtime assistance?

options.A: Measuring the exact caloric content of each food portion
options.B: Describing the spatial location of food items on a plate
options.C: Checking the temperature of hot liquids before serving
options.D: Timing how fast the patient finishes eating their meal

explanation: The clock-face method (e.g., 'your rice is at 6 o'clock and chicken at 12 o'clock') helps visually impaired patients locate their food and eat independently.

question: Your patient suddenly complains of lower back pain and chills mid-transfusion. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the symptoms unless the blood pressure drops significantly
options.B: Stop the transfusion immediately and keep the vein open with saline
options.C: Leave the room quickly to fetch the attending physician

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system react during active labour?

options.A: It stops breathing movements to rest the diaphragm
options.B: It lowers body temperature to conserve cellular fuel
options.C: It shuts down all sensory perception to force sleep
options.D: It increases heart rate, blood pressure, and energy output

question: What type of chemical messengers does the endocrine system use to communicate?

options.A: Electrolytes
options.B: Neurotransmitters
options.C: Antibodies
options.D: Hormones

question: What is a good practical habit for a breastfeeding mother to maintain proper hydration throughout the day?

question: How do intestinal parasite eggs most commonly spread to people?

question: Which nutrient is especially critical for adolescents experiencing rapid growth spurts and expanding blood volume?

question: A patient is admitted with severe heart failure and fluid accumulation in the lungs. Why is a low salt diet ordered?

question: What is the main reason for using the Z-track technique during an IM injection?

question: What usually happens to food prices when seasonal rains wash out rural transport roads?

question: Why do low-income communities often suffer more deaths during natural disasters?

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of post-abortion recovery?

question: Where do microfilariae mainly travel and live in the human body?

question: Why does the body keep the testes in the scrotum, slightly cooler than the rest of the body?

question: What is the main reason health leaders must set clear priorities in a community?

question: A ward nurse notices that the stock of intravenous cannula size 18 has fallen below the reorder level. What immediate action should be taken?

question: Why does the body use reflex actions?

options.B: To protect the body from sudden harm without conscious thought

question: Which neck position makes the submento-bregmatic diameter present itself to the birth canal?

question: What happens to the length of thin and thick filaments during muscle contraction?

question: What is Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) mainly used for in post-abortion care?

question: How do accidental and intentional poisonings usually look different when patients arrive?

options.A: Accidental cases frequently involve children and single agents, while intentional cases often involve adults and multiple drugs
options.B: Intentional poisonings are completely untreatable compared to accidental exposures

options.D: Accidental exposures never require medical attention, unlike all intentional exposures

question: Why do many follicles start growing at first, but usually only one reaches full maturity?

options.C: One dominant follicle hogs the available supply of stimulating hormones

question: In rehabilitation terms, how is a 'handicap' different from an 'impairment'?

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for adolescents living with HIV?

question: How do everyday stressors affect the development of neurasthenia?

options.B: They prevent any form of physical illness from occurring
options.C: They deplete coping reserves over time and trigger exhaustion
options.D: They have no impact on mental or physical health

question: How do daily pill organizers help improve patient medication adherence?

options.A: They chemically enhance the strength of active ingredients

options.C: They sort doses by day and time to make remembering easier
options.D: They automatically refill prescriptions at the local pharmacy

question: As a bone grows wider, its inner marrow cavity also gets bigger. Which cells are responsible for clearing out the inside?

options.A: Chondrocytes
options.B: Osteoblasts

options.D: Osteocytes

question: If someone falls into a coma from taking way too much of a drug or poison, what kind of cause is that?

options.B: Toxic and metabolic disturbances

options.D: Focal vascular ischemic strokes

question: A poorly nourished patient just started a feeding program two days ago. Will their blood albumin level shoot up right away?

question: What was a major focus of early public health pioneers like Florence Nightingale?

options.A: Hospital financial management
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug manufacturing
options.C: Advanced neurosurgical procedures
options.D: Environmental sanitation and clean water

question: A nurse does the spatula test on a baby suspected of having tetanus. What reaction confirms the diagnosis?

question: What is the most crucial safety step before placing a hot water bottle on your patient?

options.B: Testing the temperature of the water and checking the skin
options.C: Asking the patient to sign a formal surgical consent form

question: A lab report shows normal skin bacteria growing in a urine sample that was collected carelessly. What is this called?

options.A: Contamination
options.B: Immunization
options.C: Pathogenicity
options.D: Sterilization

question: A patient arrives struggling to breathe and has blue lips after inhaling toxic fumes. What is your very first nursing priority?

options.A: Ask family members what chemical was spilled
options.B: Draw blood samples for a complete blood count
options.C: Ensure a patent airway and provide high-flow oxygen
options.D: Document the exact time of the workplace accident

question: What kind of organism causes paragonimiasis?

options.B: A blood parasite

question: Why is overfilling a sharps safety box a dangerous hazard?

options.C: It automatically dissolves the cardboard exterior

question: Which level of healthcare prevention includes traditional rehabilitation activities?

question: What is the best dietary advice for a patient recovering from a bout of diarrhoea?

question: Why do nurses need to keep checking updated clinical guidelines for managing reproductive health issues?

question: Which environmental strategy helps manage a confused and restless patient experiencing delirium?

question: How do old myths and bad ideas about the causes of physical disability affect people in the community?

question: Which nursing action is vital for preventing joint stiffness (contractures) in a bedridden patient?

question: Why can it be tricky to diagnose a parasite based only on general complaints like fatigue or tummy ache?

question: What should a nurse tell a patient to expect regarding bleeding after taking these medications?

question: What does the handy acronym AFASS help healthcare workers figure out about infant feeding?

options.A: The nutritional content of expressed breast milk
options.B: The rate of viral clearance in a nursing mother
options.C: The exact dosage of infant antiretroviral medications
options.D: The safety and suitability of replacement formula feeding

explanation: AFASS is a great tool! It checks if formula feeding is Affordable, Feasible, Acceptable, Sustainable, and Safe for the family's real-life situation.

question: According to global health guidelines, how long should an infant be exclusively breastfed?

options.A: For the first six months of life
options.B: For the first three months only
options.C: Until the infant starts walking
options.D: Until the baby cuts their first tooth

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives babies the absolute best start, providing all the water, food, and immune protection they need!

question: What is the main job of ATP when it binds to myosin during muscle contraction?

options.A: To allow the myosin head to detach from actin
options.B: To release acetylcholine into the synapse
options.C: To pull the Z-lines further apart
options.D: To instantly activate the sarcoplasmic reticulum

explanation: ATP is the energy currency that acts like a release button, letting the myosin head disconnect from actin so it can reset for the next pull. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why is a pregnancy test almost always ordered when a patient arrives with lower belly pain and suspected salpingitis?

options.A: To confirm that the patient is currently using hormonal contraceptives
options.B: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy, which can present with similar pain
options.C: To measure baseline kidney function before starting antibiotic therapy
options.D: To check if high hormone levels caused the bacterial overgrowth

explanation: An ectopic pregnancy is a medical emergency that can mimic pelvic infection pain, so nurses always check this first to keep the patient safe.

question: What do you call the high-pitched, musical breathing sound that tells you there is a partial blockage in the upper airway?

options.A: Wheezes
options.B: Stridor
options.C: Crackles
options.D: Rhonchi

explanation: Brilliant! Stridor is that harsh, high-pitched sound you hear when air is struggling to squeeze past a narrow or blocked upper airway (like the larynx or trachea).

question: In the very first hour after delivery (the fourth stage), how often should you check the mother's vital signs and womb tone?

options.A: Every 4 hours
options.B: Every 15 minutes
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every hour

explanation: Keep shining! Because the risk of bleeding is highest right after birth, we monitor her closely every 15 minutes during that first hour.

question: Which part of the inner ear turns sound vibrations into electrical signals for the brain?

options.A: Cochlea
options.B: Tympanic membrane
options.C: Malleus
options.D: Auditory canal

explanation: The cochlea is shaped like a little snail shell. It is packed with fluid and tiny hair cells that translate physical sound waves into nerve impulses.

question: A nurse notices that a surgical drain has produced 300 mL of bright red blood in the last hour. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Strip the tubing vigorously to clear out any remaining blood clots
options.B: Elevate the collection bag above the level of the patient's wound
options.C: Document the normal finding and check the patient again tomorrow
options.D: Notify the surgeon immediately because this suggests active hemorrhage

explanation: A sudden, large volume of bright red drainage indicates heavy bleeding inside the body, which requires urgent medical intervention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way to handle cultural diversity in learning?

options.A: Understanding that cultural backgrounds shape views on health and authority
options.B: Assuming every student learns and communicates in the exact same way
options.C: Recognizing diverse viewpoints to enrich classroom discussions
options.D: Creating a space where different communication styles are respected

explanation: Remember, we are all unique! Educators must embrace student diversity rather than expecting everyone to learn through a single mold.

question: How should a nurse leader respond when frontline staff push back against a new QI project?

options.A: Force immediate compliance without offering any explanation
options.B: Report them immediately to hospital human resources for insubordination
options.C: Listen to their concerns with empathy to find practical flaws
options.D: Ignore the complaints because resistance always fades away

explanation: That's right! Staff pushback often points out real problems in the daily workflow that leadership missed. It's helpful feedback, not just stubbornness.

question: If a patient cannot speak, which physical sign might tell you they are in pain?

options.A: Deep, slow, and relaxed breathing
options.B: Low blood pressure and calm posture
options.C: Tachycardia and facial grimacing
options.D: Warm and dry skin on the hands

explanation: Spot on! When patients can't talk, their body speaks for them—look out for a fast heart rate (tachycardia) and tight, frowning facial expressions.

question: A patient asks why their shoulder can move in circles while their elbow can only bend and straighten. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: The elbow contains more synovial fluid
options.B: The shoulder has much stronger muscles
options.C: The different shapes of the joint structures control the movement
options.D: The shoulder has softer bones than the elbow

explanation: You got it! Structure dictates function. A ball-and-socket shape lets the shoulder rotate, while a hinge shape restricts the elbow to one plane.

question: Which Nigerian agency leads the fight against drug trafficking and abuse?

options.A: Frsc
options.B: Nafdac
options.C: Nysc
options.D: NDLEA

explanation: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) is the main body responsible for tackling illicit drug crimes in Nigeria.

question: What is a main goal of visiting a mother at home during the postnatal period?

options.A: To evaluate the household income level and financial status
options.B: To perform minor surgical operations on the mother
options.C: To monitor uterine involution and check maternal vital signs
options.D: To administer routine adult vaccinations to the father

explanation: Postnatal visits let you make sure the womb is shrinking back down nicely (involution) and that the mother's blood pressure and temperature are safe.

question: Why is it important to rest your fingers against the patient's cheek while holding the otoscope?

options.A: To block out bright room lighting for a clearer visual field
options.B: To prevent injury to the ear canal if the patient suddenly moves
options.C: To keep the otoscope battery handle from becoming disconnected
options.D: To warm up the speculum before it touches the sensitive skin

explanation: Bracing your hand on their cheek is a brilliant safety trick. If the patient jerks or moves, your hand moves with them, protecting the delicate ear canal!

question: When opening a sterile pack, which part of the sterile drape or wrapper is always considered contaminated?

options.A: The portion closest to the patient
options.B: The top surface facing upwards
options.C: The outer one-inch border
options.D: The exact center of the drape

explanation: Spot on! That outer edge touches non-sterile surfaces when packaged, so we always treat the outer one-inch margin as unsterile.

question: A nurse sighs loudly and makes a rude comment while cleaning up a PAC patient. Which nursing rule was broken?

options.A: Objective, non-judgmental communication
options.B: Aseptic surgical technique
options.C: Accurate medication dosage calculation
options.D: Emergency triage prioritization

explanation: Making disapproving remarks or sighs shames the patient and completely breaks the rule of giving non-judgmental, professional care.

question: What happens when a tumor suppressor gene experiences a loss-of-function mutation?

options.A: The cell immediately transforms into a benign fibrous cyst
options.B: The cell loses its molecular brakes and divides uncontrollably
options.C: The cell creates an outer capsule to prevent metastasis
options.D: Normal cellular division stops permanently in the G0 phase

explanation: Tumor suppressor genes normally slow down cell growth; losing them removes these protective brakes, allowing rapid tumor growth. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h6)

question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

options.A: A termination done by unskilled persons or in unsterile environments
options.B: A surgical procedure performed strictly in a teaching hospital
options.C: Any termination of pregnancy requested by a minor
options.D: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally before the twentieth week

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means a procedure done without proper medical skills, sterile tools, or safe standards. Always look out for the setting and who is performing it.

question: What is a frequent, painful problem caused by excessive pushing during bowel movements in pregnancy?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Hemorrhoids

explanation: You got it! Straining puts heavy pressure on the pelvic veins, which often leads to swollen, painful hemorrhoids (piles).

question: What practical method do community health nurses use while moving through a neighborhood to observe living conditions?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Windshield survey
options.C: Biopsy screening
options.D: Laboratory blood analysis

explanation: Correct! A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse travels through a community to spot living conditions and local resources. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h4)

question: A newborn at home is limp, blue, and not breathing well even after being dried. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if color returns
options.B: Initiate positive pressure ventilation using a neonatal resuscitation bag
options.C: Administer oral sugar water to the infant
options.D: Wrap the baby tightly and hand it to the grandmother

explanation: When a baby is floppy and not breathing, every second counts. Start bag-valve-mask ventilation right away to help them breathe.

question: A home health nurse visits a patient with chronic heart failure. Which action best supports long-term disease management?

options.A: Advising the patient to eat as much salted food as they want
options.B: Telling the patient to stop taking all prescribed daily water pills
options.C: Teaching the patient how to weigh themselves daily and track swelling
options.D: Discharging the patient from care because the disease is ongoing

explanation: Daily weight tracking helps catch fluid retention early before it turns into a dangerous heart failure flare-up. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which physical sign is a classic telltale clue of an opioid overdose?

options.A: Excessive sweating
options.B: High fever
options.C: Pinpoint pupils
options.D: Wide dilated pupils

explanation: Spotting tiny, constricted pupils (miosis) is one of the classic physical signs that instantly helps nurses suspect an opioid overdose in the ward.

question: A patient recovering from abdominal surgery has not passed gas or had a bowel movement in three days. Which basic need is primarily affected?

options.A: Elimination
options.B: Safety and security
options.C: Love and belonging
options.D: Self-esteem

explanation: Bowel function falls under physiological elimination needs, which nurses closely monitor post-operatively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: A woman's last menstrual period began on January 1st. Using Naegele's rule, what is her estimated date of delivery (EDD)?

options.A: September 15th
options.B: November 5th
options.C: October 8th
options.D: December 25th

explanation: Easy trick: add 7 days to the first day of the last period, then subtract 3 months. Jan 1st + 7 days = Jan 8th, minus 3 months = October 8th!

question: What prompted the creation of formal critical care nursing organizations and certification standards?

options.A: The complete elimination of physicians from intensive care units
options.B: A government mandate to reduce the total number of working hospital nurses
options.C: The increasing complexity of patient technology requiring advanced specialized skills
options.D: A sudden drop in the number of students applying to nursing school

explanation: General training could not keep pace with advanced monitors and life support, leading to the creation of specialized critical care nursing standards. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the recommended chest compression rate per minute for an adult in cardiac arrest?

options.A: 140 to 160 compressions per minute
options.B: 100 to 120 compressions per minute
options.C: 60 to 80 compressions per minute
options.D: 40 to 60 compressions per minute

explanation: A rate of 100 to 120 per minute mimics a normal working heart rate to push blood forward effectively. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why do patients experience shortness of breath when they have a respiratory problem?

options.A: The kidneys are retaining too much water
options.B: The heart is pumping too much blood to the muscles
options.C: The stomach is pushing upward against the diaphragm
options.D: The body is trying to fix low oxygen or high carbon dioxide levels

explanation: Think of shortness of breath as an alarm bell! It's your body's clever way of telling you it needs more oxygen or needs to blow off extra carbon dioxide. Great effort!

question: What is an effective community nursing strategy to help stop FGM?

options.A: Inspecting every household's private rooms every single week
options.B: Punishing mothers publicly for crimes committed by elders
options.C: Banning all community meetings and traditional gatherings in villages
options.D: Promoting alternative rites of passage that celebrate maturity without cutting

explanation: Spot on! Offering safe, positive ways to celebrate cultural milestones helps communities keep their traditions alive while dropping the dangerous cutting.

question: A patient is staring blankly, speaking very little, and showing no emotion after an accident. What are they likely experiencing?

options.A: Aggressive hostility
options.B: Emotional numbness
options.C: Delusional psychosis
options.D: Hyper-arousal panic

explanation: Spot on! Right after trauma, a patient's mind can freeze up or go numb, making them look quiet, blank, and detached.

question: What is the correct immediate action when a nurse discovers a vital sign monitor has a broken power cord?

options.A: Continue using it with the broken wire taped up
options.B: Hide it inside the nurse's locker until the manager returns
options.C: Throw it directly into the black domestic waste bin
options.D: Label it out of service and report it for repair

explanation: Faulty electrical equipment poses severe hazards and must be removed from use and reported right away. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which method involves a nurse driving or walking through an area to observe living conditions firsthand?

options.A: Random clinical trial
options.B: Windshield survey
options.C: Laboratory blood screening
options.D: Surgical audit

explanation: Well done! Think of a windshield survey like taking a mental snapshot through a car window—you are out there observing housing, roads, and everyday life.

question: When patients engage in emotional eating, what is usually driving the habit?

options.A: Stress, boredom, or anxiety
options.B: Lack of clean drinking water
options.C: High environmental temperatures
options.D: Low physical activity levels

explanation: Correct! Many people reach for snacks not because they are genuinely hungry, but to comfort themselves when feeling stressed, anxious, or bored.

question: When do pregnant women most commonly start experiencing symptoms of constipation?

options.A: Early in the first trimester
options.B: Only during active labor
options.C: Right after delivery occurs
options.D: Exclusively in the final week

explanation: Great job! Hormonal shifts happen right from the start of pregnancy, which is why tummy troubles often pop up early in the first trimester.

question: A patient getting a fast IV infusion of vancomycin suddenly has a red face and neck. What's going on?

options.A: An acute allergic reaction requiring epinephrine
options.B: Severe liver failure due to drug overdose
options.C: Red Man Syndrome caused by infusion rate
options.D: Normal therapeutic effectiveness of the drug

explanation: Classic Red Man Syndrome! It happens when vancomycin goes in too fast and histamine is released. Don't panic—just slow down the infusion rate as ordered.

question: Why is it usually recommended to take oral corticosteroid pills with meals or food?

options.A: To speed up the absorption of the drug through the intestinal wall
options.B: To completely eliminate the risk of developing systemic fluid retention
options.C: To minimize stomach irritation and reduce the risk of gastrointestinal ulcers
options.D: To prevent the medication from altering the patient's morning blood glucose

explanation: Steroids can be tough on the stomach lining and increase acid. Taking them with food acts like a cozy blanket to protect the stomach from irritation and ulcers.

question: Which condition would most likely lead to a client being denied admission to a standard adult day care center?

options.A: Using a walker or cane for safe indoor mobility
options.B: Needing assistance with eating meals during the day
options.C: Mild forgetfulness associated with early-stage aging
options.D: Severe, unpredictable physical aggression toward others

explanation: Uncontrolled aggressive behaviors pose safety risks to staff and other participants, making standard day care settings unsuitable unless specialized behavioral resources exist. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why is peer support so encouraging for someone newly diagnosed with a permanent physical disability?

options.A: It prevents family members from interfering in treatment decisions
options.B: It replaces the need for professional nursing care and medications
options.C: It connects them with someone who truly understands their lived experience
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will regain full physical movement

explanation: Nothing beats talking to someone who has walked in your shoes. Peer mentors offer real hope and practical tips that textbooks just can't match.

question: A patient starting HIV treatment is worried about forgetting their daily pills. What is a helpful nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking the pills if they feel well
options.B: Help the patient set up phone reminders and a pill organizer
options.C: Suggest that missing a few doses per month has no real effect
options.D: Advise the patient to take a double dose whenever one is missed

explanation: Simple tools like daily pill boxes and phone alarms are fantastic practical ways to help patients stick to their routine.

question: When we say a daily diet has "adequacy," what does that mainly mean?

options.A: Consuming fewer calories than you burn each day
options.B: Limiting your food intake to only one meal type
options.C: Buying expensive imported food items regularly
options.D: Eating enough essential nutrients to meet bodily needs

explanation: Spot on! Adequacy simply means your diet gives you enough energy and all the vital nutrients your body needs to stay healthy and strong.
